title: Record of Deportable / Inadmissible Alien
spanishTitle: Expediente de un extranjero expulsable o inadmisible
purpose: The I-213 serves as DHS' and its sub-agencies' 'source of truth' regarding a given person that they consider deportable. The information in the 213 is used to create the NTA itself, and often comes up during immigration proceedings when an individual fails to appear for a hearing. At that point, the DHS representative present at court has to file an updated I-213 with the Court in order for the IJ to act upon a request for in absentia removal from DHS counsel for failure to appear.
notes: Not filed by applicants. Often mentioned in fast-moving procedural conversations between Counsel and the IJ.

title: Notice of Referral to Immigration Judge
spanishTitle: Aviso de remisión ante un juez de inmigración
purpose: The I-863 is a less commonly used form than some; it is a sort of charging document, as it has a similar effect to an NTA, in that the named person is placed in EOIR proceedings. As per the relevant statute (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-235/section-235.6), this can be, for example, following a credible fear interview, when credible fear is not found; when someone is suspected to be faking their legal status, and other situations, as well.
notes: Unlikely to come up outside of EOIR; if you hear it at USCIS, that's a bad day.

title: Additional Charges of Inadmissibility / Deportability
spanishTitle: Imputaciones adicionales de inadmisibilidad o expulsabilidad
purpose: The I-261 is used to add, amend, or otherwise modify the NTA in a given case. This can include adding new charges, correcting factual bases, or otherwise modifying the document. This is an entirely internal form; there don't even appear to be many images of it available online. It played an important role in the Saga of 'what is a notice to appear, anyway?'; for more on this, see Niz-Chavez, here: https://gringo.bingo/#/legal-authority

title: Application for Advance Permission to Enter as a Nonimmigrant
spanishTitle: Solicitud de permiso anticipado para entrar como no inmigrante
purpose: The I-192 is a document that might end up in a Record of Proceedings, but it's not commonly used inside the US. Instead, it is used most often in embassies or consulates abroad wherein someone is requesting that previous immigration history -- something that happened that made them 'inadmissible' -- be waived so that they may enter the country legally.

title: Notice of Intent/Decision to Reinstate Prior Order
spanishTitle: Aviso de intención o auto de restablecimiento de una orden previa
purpose: Yet another charging document, the I-871 is specific to the circumstances of someone who has previously been removed from the country, or at least, had an order of removal against them, left the country, and has entered the country again, and is thereby being placed in removal proceedings.

title: Arrival/Departure Record
purpose: This is that piece of paper they give you on the airplane before you land. Or when you're paroled into the country. It's a record of someone entering or leaving the country if they're not a citizen.
notes: The I-94 is involved in the parole process, from the point of view of the parolee; however, it's not the actual form that does the parole; that would be USCIS form I-131.

title: Request for Social Security Earnings Information
spanishTitle: Solicitud de información sobre ingresos registrados por el Seguro Social
purpose: Requests the record of earnings declared by, or attributable to, a particular individual.
notes: While not an immigration form, and highly rare in the immigratoin context, it may come up e.g. if someone is trying to prove lawful presence in the country, either their own or that of a relative e.g. in order to obtain derivative or inherited status.

title: Notice of Custody Determination
purpose: An internal DHS document that serves as notice and declaration of a custody decision regarding an individual.
notes: Most often, this would be determining that they should be detained without bond; however, if they are granted a bond, or even granted the option to have bond e.g. through a class habeus case, another I-286 may be filed to reflect that change.

title: Application for Certificate of Citizenship
purpose: Does what it says on the tin: this form requests a certification of citizenship. It doesn't change anything about the citizenship, merely serves to verify the citizenship exists.
notes: Again, pretty rare, and to my knowledge, not something an IJ could find on; however, it could come up in cases involving derived or inherited citizenship, wherein someone is trying to prove that they're related to a citizen. Or in disputed removability proceedings.
